samples.summary: Shift+click cell-range parity is only implemented for top-level tables, leaving the nested-table case (the very case the other half of this PR fixes) still collapsing the caret
samples.evidence: The new arm is guarded by `anchorCellInfo && anchorCellInfo.tableBlockId === pos.blockId`, where `pos.blockId` is necessarily a TOP-LEVEL table block (the enclosing branch resolves `clickedBlock` from `this.doc.document.blocks.find(...)`, text-editor.ts:2023-2025). For an anchor inside a NESTED table, `anchorCellInfo.tableBlockId` is the inner table id, so the condition is false and control falls to the pre-existing `else` that moves the caret and clears the selection (2104-2108). The drag path handles exactly this case explicitly — `resolvedCellInfo.tableBlockId === anchorTableId` → "Different cell in the SAME table (e.g., inner table cell-range selection)" (2399-2417) — and also handles the outer-table fallback via `findOuterCellAddress` (2418-2431), neither of which the shift+click arm mirrors. The task plan's acceptance (docs/tasks/active/20260914-table-drag-merge-selection-todo.md:46-47, "shift+click across rows produces the same rectangle as the equivalent drag") therefore holds only for top-level tables; a user shift+clicking across cells of a nested table still gets no cell range, which is the same gesture/nesting mismatch #1049 is about.
searchedFor: new test file table-drag-merge-selection.test.ts uses only a top-level `insertTable`

samples.summary: Cell-range construction is copy-pasted a fourth time instead of reusing the drag path's builder — the exact divergence the change's own lessons doc warns about
samples.evidence: The same shape (`expandCellRangeForMerges({blockId, start: anchor cell, end: clicked cell}, this.doc.getBlock(id).tableData!)` followed by a selection write) now exists at text-editor.ts:2090 (new), 2404, 2424 and 3367. Because the new copy re-derives the table id and address resolution by hand rather than reusing the drag path's logic, it already diverges from it (no inner-table / outer-cell resolution). docs/tasks/active/20260914-table-drag-merge-selection-lessons.md:30-32 states the rule this violates: "When two neighbours resolve the same thing two ways, the weaker one is a latent bug; unify on the one that already handles the general case." A shared `buildCellRangeSelection(anchorBlockId, clickedCellAddr)` helper would keep shift+click and drag from answering the same question two ways.

samples.summary: The selection.ts fix keeps both lookups rather than unifying on the general one, so the double-resolution it was meant to remove is still there
samples.evidence: `resolveNestedTableLayout` already returns the top-level table itself when `topTableId === tableBlockId` (table-layout.ts:490-500), so the retained `layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === crBlockId)?.block.tableData ??` prefix is redundant except in the corner case where a top-level table block has `tableData` but no `layoutTable`. Every other call site in this file (selection.ts:169, 299, 590) uses `resolveNestedTableLayout` alone. Keeping the flat lookup as the primary leaves two resolution rules for one table — the stated defect — in place, just with a fallback bolted on.

samples.summary: New shift+click cell-range gesture is not recorded in the tables design doc, whose Selection section still describes cell-range selection as drag-only
samples.evidence: docs-tables.md:251-257 ("### Selection") says "Drag across a cell boundary switches to cell-range selection" and the navigation table at 241-249 lists Tab/Shift+Tab/arrows/Cmd+A but no shift+click. CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16,59-61 requires the canonical subsystem doc to be updated for a non-trivial behavior change; this PR adds a user-visible gesture (shift+click builds a merge-expanded `tableCellRange`) and updates no design doc. Cost stays inside the codebase (behavior works as specified), hence minor.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: the shift+click cell-range arm at text-editor.ts:2084 is guarded by `anchorCellInfo.tableBlockId === pos.blockId`, and `pos.blockId` is restricted to top-level body blocks by the enclosing lookup at 2023 (`this.doc.document.blocks.find`). `getCellInfo` (3832-3837) is a raw `blockParentMap.get`, so an anchor inside a nested table yields the inner table id, the guard fails, and control reaches the `else` at 2104-2108 which moves the caret and clears the selection; the first arm (2070-2083) compares only row/col and yields a cross-cell text range that `normalizeRange` discards as invalid (selection.ts:161-179). The drag path by contrast handles both nested sub-cases explicitly (2360-2365 outermost walk, 2399-2417 inner-table range, 2418-2438 `findOuterCellAddress` outer range, with nested descent in `resolveOffsetInCellAtXY` at 5673-5709). I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: every `shiftKey` occurrence in packages/docs/src (only 2065 and 2153 are pointer paths), the single `mousedown` registration (770 → handleMouseDown 1854; editor.ts:3111 is the image-handle capture listener), and every `tableCellRange` construction site in the tree (text-editor.ts:2090 shift+click, 2404/2424 drag, 3367 shift+arrow keyboard) — none is a nested-aware shift+click, and no test covers one. Blocking under the design-fit lens because the task plan's acceptance (docs/tasks/active/20260914-table-drag-merge-selection-todo.md:36-38,46-47) is unqualified about table nesting while the companion half of this change (selection.ts:120-136) exists precisely to fix the nested case of #1049, so the stated drag/shift+click parity outcome does not hold for a user inside a nested table.
